newsitem.title: CHINA: China may deregulate oil prices as early as 1998.
newsitem.headline: China may deregulate oil prices as early as 1998.

text.p: China may deregulate prices of domestic crude to bring them into line with international levels as early as 1998, the China Economic Times said on Friday, quoting the Ministry of Internal Trade.
The price of crude oil would most likely rise this year because the government planned to raise domestic crude prices to world price levels in 1998, it said.
Oil product prices would also rise, it said.
Prices of diesel and petrol on the open market in the first quarter had already increased and the rise in the price of petrol had been higher than that for diesel, it said, but gave no details.
China controls its domestic oil prices but has gradually relaxed the restrictions in recent years.
China last raised its domestic crude oil price by 86.1 yuan ($10.3) per tonne in December and moved its diesel prices up 200 yuan to 2,190 yuan per tonne and gasoline by 100 yuan to 2,280 yuan.
